knowledge:
- key_parameters: dataList=A list of matrices from different data types where rows represent samples and columns represent features ;; seed=Integer seed for reproducibility ;; ncores=Number of cores for parallel processing ;; trainList=List of matrices for training dataset in risk prediction ;; testList=List of matrices for testing dataset in risk prediction ;; trainSurvival=A Surv object containing survival time and event status for the training set
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: When performing cancer subtyping or patient risk score prediction using high-dimensional multi-omics datasets (e.g., mRNA, miRNA, methylation) where noise reduction and robust consensus clustering are required.
- pitfalls: Requires C++ libtorch via the torch package; if not automatically installed, users must run torch::install_torch() manually. Survival times must be positive when predicting risk scores (e.g., adjusting survival time via survival$Survival - min(survival$Survival) + 1).

workflows.name: multi_omics_subtyping
workflows.intent: Identify robust disease subtypes from multi-omics data using consensus factor analysis.
input: dataList (a list of matrices, each representing a molecular data type with samples as rows and features as columns)
survival (a data frame containing survival time and event status for the samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SCFA and survival packages ;; 2. Prepare the multi-omics data list ;; 3. Run the SCFA function to generate subtype assignments ;; 4. Perform survival analysis using coxph to evaluate the clinical significance of the subtypes.
workflows.code:
library(SCFA)
library(survival)
data("GBM")
dataList <- GBM$data
survival <- GBM$survival
set.seed(1)
subtype <- SCFA(dataList, seed = 1, ncores = 4L)
coxFit <- coxph(Surv(time = Survival, event = Death) ~ as.factor(subtype), data = survival, ties="exact")
coxP <- round(summary(coxFit)$sctest[3],digits = 20)
print(coxP)

workflows.name: risk_score_prediction
workflows.intent: Predict patient risk scores using survival information from training data and multi-omics profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SCFA and survival packages ;; 2. Prepare training and testing multi-omics data lists and survival objects (ensuring survival times are positive) ;; 3. Run the SCFA.class function to predict risk scores for the test set ;; 4. Validate the predicted risk scores using the concordance index.
workflows.code:
library(SCFA)
library(survival)
data("GBM")
dataList <- GBM$data
survival <- GBM$survival
set.seed(1)
idx <- sample.int(nrow(dataList[[1]]), round(nrow(dataList[[1]])/2) )
survival$Survival <- survival$Survival - min(survival$Survival) + 1
trainList <- lapply(dataList, function(x) x[idx, ] )
trainSurvival <- Surv(time = survival[idx,]$Survival, event =  survival[idx,]$Death)
testList <- lapply(dataList, function(x) x[-idx, ] )
testSurvival <- Surv(time = survival[-idx,]$Survival, event =  survival[-idx,]$Death)
result <- SCFA.class(trainList, trainSurvival, testList, seed = 1, ncores = 4L)
c.index <- survival::concordance(coxph(testSurvival ~ result))$concordance
print(c.index)
